business: Docketra (B2B Practice Operations Platform for Indian CAs & CSs)
why_not: Even with restricted Google Drive permissions, letting any third-party tool connect to our client repository is too much of a confidentiality risk for sensitive ITR and ROC records. Furthermore, as a two-person practice with rotating article trainees, training them on new software is a waste of time when our manual folders suffice.

I have run our practice on spreadsheets and WhatsApp for ten years, and I cannot trust a setup where an assistant might accidentally move or delete our Google Drive folders. With a mid-sized team and rotating clerks, the risk of accidental deletions or misplaced client archives is too great to risk our operations on new software.
At ₹12,990 a year, it is still double the cost of Jamku, so as a frugal firm we would rather test the free sandbox with one trainee on 5 clients first before paying anything.

With 10 staff we exceed the 5-user Starter plan, and jumping straight to the Pro Tier at ₹4,999 a month billed annually forces an upfront commitment of nearly ₹60,000. That is far too steep for my frugal practice to risk without testing team adoption first.

My article clerks rotate every couple of years, and I cannot spend precious billable hours training new batches on yet another software portal. In an ordinary week, if a tool requires onboarding effort, my staff will just revert to WhatsApp and the subscription will sit unused.

I am eager to automate our morning WhatsApp document flood, but my article clerks rotate every couple of years and retraining them on a complex operating system is an ongoing drain. Until adoption is completely effortless for fresh trainees without partner handholding, I cannot justify paying for an annual subscription.

I've run my practice on WhatsApp and Excel for ten years without paying a rupee, so getting my staff to adopt a new platform sounds like an uphill battle. If I test this at all, I'll stick to the free sandbox before I ever consider paying ₹12,990 a year.

I have run our practice on spreadsheets and WhatsApp groups for ten years at zero software cost, and my team's habits are set in stone. Asking us to adopt a new system with a ₹12,990 annual commitment introduces friction we simply do not need when our current setup works fine.
As a solo CA with just one trainee, our workload fits within manual routines and the free sandbox; I have no operational need to spend ₹12,990 a year on a 5-user plan.

In an ordinary week outside the July ITR or October ROC rush, I'm not going to spend ₹12,990 upfront when my clients just dump bills on WhatsApp anyway. I only pull the trigger on software when deadline panic or peer-review pressure forces my hand, so right now I would at most test the free sandbox.
why_yes: At ₹12,990 a year with no setup fees or per-user nickeling, it is affordable enough to fix my daily morning triage across 30 WhatsApp client groups while keeping files safe under restricted drive.file scope.

At ₹12,990 a year flat for up to 5 seats with no per-user fees or setup charges, it covers our whole 4-person team affordably, and letting clients keep dumping documents on WhatsApp without forcing them into a portal solves my morning triage across 30 client groups.

Checking 30 WhatsApp client groups every morning before tea is my biggest operational bottleneck, and automating triage into structured dockets without forcing clients into a portal while keeping our Drive safe under restricted drive.file scope makes this an easy purchase.
